seo.title: AI SQL assistant and local MCP server
seo.description: Explain, optimize and fix SQL with the AI provider you choose, and let MCP clients such as Claude Code use saved connections through a local MCP server.

header.title: AI assistant and MCP
header.lead: Ask about your database with the AI provider you choose, and let AI clients work with saved connections through MCP (Model Context Protocol).

bands.title: Choose your AI provider
text: Use {aiProviders} with an API key, an account or a local model. Requests go straight to the provider; TablePro runs no AI service. The assistant is free, and your provider may charge.
From the editor, review, explain or optimize a statement, or fix one that failed. Nothing runs, and a suggestion reaches the editor only when you apply it.
notes: Result rows stay out of messages unless you allow them in <ui>Settings > AI</ui>. Linux supports {aiProvidersLinux}.

bands.title: Chat modes and Agent mode
text: Ask, the default, reads the schema and runs nothing. Edit runs queries, and Agent can also propose destructive statements, under the connection’s Safe Mode: Alert and stricter levels confirm writes, Read-Only refuses them. Full-window Agent mode keeps the connection at Alert or stricter while it works.

bands.title: Connect AI clients through MCP
text: The built-in MCP server lets clients such as {mcpSetupClients} use your saved connections without seeing their passwords. It is off until you turn it on, listens on {mcpHost} only, and logs every call.
Each call passes the token’s scope, the connection’s External Clients level, its approval setting and Safe Mode, and the strictest one wins.
notes: On Linux the server offers {mcpToolCountLinux} tools, over HTTP.

more.title: External MCP tools
text: The assistant can call an outside MCP server over Streamable HTTP. Every tool call waits for your click.

more.title: Automation
text: AppleScript, tablepro:// links and the Raycast extension open connections and run queries, within each connection’s limits.

more.title: Where your data goes
text: Prompts and schema go to your provider under its terms, or stay on your machine with a local model. TablePro receives none of it.
